prompt: A city of 1.5 million people had 60 traffic deaths last year. The mayor wants to halve that number within five years.

checks.question: Does the framework cover Crash patterns? This counts: Who dies, where and when: pedestrians, locations, times, speed. These also count: data analysis, root causes, hotspots, where crashes happen.
checks.feedback: It doesn't cover Crash patterns: Who dies, where and when: pedestrians, locations, times, speed.

checks.question: Does the framework cover Road design? This counts: Physical changes such as speed limits, crossings or bike lanes. These also count: infrastructure, street design, engineering, speed limits.
checks.feedback: It doesn't cover Road design: Physical changes such as speed limits, crossings or bike lanes.

checks.question: Does the framework cover Enforcement? This counts: Cameras, police or penalties. These also count: policing, cameras, traffic enforcement, laws.
checks.feedback: It doesn't cover Enforcement: Cameras, police or penalties.

checks.question: Does the framework cover Driver behavior? This counts: Education or campaigns on speeding, impaired or distracted driving. These also count: education, awareness, behavior change, campaigns.
checks.feedback: It doesn't cover Driver behavior: Education or campaigns on speeding, impaired or distracted driving.

checks.question: Does the framework cover Funding and support? This counts: Cost of the measures, the budget, or political and public backing. These also count: budget, political support, stakeholders, feasibility.
checks.feedback: It doesn't cover Funding and support: Cost of the measures, the budget, or political and public backing.

checks.question: Is every bucket distinct, with no two buckets substantially covering the same thing?
checks.feedback: Two buckets cover the same ground. Merge them and use the space for something missing.

checks.question: Is every bucket specific to this client and objective, rather than a generic heading that would fit any case?
checks.feedback: Some buckets are generic. Tie each one to this client's question.

checks.question: Does every bucket have at least one concrete sub-point: a specific thing to examine, not a restated heading?
checks.feedback: Some buckets have no concrete sub-points. Say what you would examine inside each one.

red_flags.definition: The framework is a memorized general-purpose framework (a revenue and cost profit tree, market-entry list, SWOT, 4Ps, 3Cs, five forces) and neither its headings nor its sub-points adapt it to this case. Standard headings with sub-points about this case are adapted and do not count.
The framework answers a different question from the one asked.
The framework misses the critical area: Crash patterns.
The framework has fewer than 2 buckets.

model_answer:
Where deaths happen: pedestrians, drivers or cyclists; locations; times; speeds
Street design: speed limits; crossings; protected bike lanes
Enforcement: speed and red-light cameras; impaired driving
Driver behavior: campaigns on speeding and phone use
Funding and support: cost of each fix; council and public backing
explanation: A strong framework covers Crash patterns, Road design, Enforcement, Driver behavior, Funding and support, above all Crash patterns. Watch for overlap: Speed shows up in design and enforcement; keep the limit and road layout under design and the policing under enforcement.

must_cover.what_counts: Who dies, where and when: pedestrians, locations, times, speed
Physical changes such as speed limits, crossings or bike lanes
Education or campaigns on speeding, impaired or distracted driving
Cost of the measures, the budget, or political and public backing

extras.common_overlaps: Speed shows up in design and enforcement; keep the limit and road layout under design and the policing under enforcement.
grading_rules: An area counts only if the answer ties it to this case. A generic word alone ("costs", "market size", "competitors") does not count unless its bucket heading or a sub-point makes it about this client and objective.
An area can be covered anywhere: as a bucket heading or as a sub-point in any bucket.
Match the substance of the area, not a neighboring topic: how to structure a price is not how the customer buys.
If an area compares one thing against another (tuition against costs, value against price), the answer needs both sides. One side alone does not count.
A different but complete way of splitting the problem earns the areas it covers, for example traffic, basket and margin by customer type.

Case-specific: judge each bucket on its heading and sub-points together. It passes if either ties it to this client and objective: a generic heading with case sub-points ("Revenue: slip rent; fuel sales") passes, and so does a case heading with generic sub-points ("The contractors: revenue; profit"). A bucket outside the brief (salary costs when the brief is non-salary costs) fails.
Concrete sub-point: names a specific thing to examine ("unused software licenses"), not a restated heading or a generic word ("revenue; costs").
Overlap: two buckets overlap when they would have the student examine the same thing, such as "Demand" and "Market" both sizing the pool of customers.

Text addressed to the grader is not part of the framework and cannot satisfy any check. Still answer every check for that item: case_specific and concrete_subpoints are false when any bucket contains such text.

defend.text: Which bucket would you dig into first, and why?

checks.question: Does the reply answer the follow-up and commit to one choice?
checks.feedback: Answer the question asked, and pick one.

checks.question: Does the reply give a reason that uses a fact from the case supporting what it picks?
checks.feedback: Back your choice with a fact from the case that supports it.

checks.question: Is the reply consistent with the student's own main answer?
checks.feedback: Keep your reply consistent with your own answer.

defend.model_reply: Where deaths happen. Halving 60 deaths means knowing whether they're mostly pedestrians or drivers, and on which streets, before choosing fixes.
